claims.text: Percona's 2019 self-managed MongoDB 3.6.12 reproduction causes a WiredTiger panic by changing data-file ownership. Its preceding storage message reports Permission denied. This is a counterexample to treating every WiredTiger panic or fatal assertion as proof of on-disk corruption requiring restore or resynchronization. (low confidence)

MongoDB's error-code reference and server definitions identify code 50 as MaxTimeMSExpired; the original claim that it means a plan-cache error is incorrect. The server definition places it in Interruption and ExceededTimeLimitError categories. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Code 11600 is InterruptedAtShutdown. A Bitnami chart issue contains this error during documented SIGTERM and shutdown-command sequences. Therefore this code alone cannot establish an OOM kill, crash, maintenance event or the actor that initiated shutdown; that causal attribution requires separate evidence. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

An invariant failure involving WiredTiger does not by itself prove media bit rot or a corrupted block header. Percona's historical PSMDB-28 fix addresses an invariant failure during sparse-index creation; its stack-trace walkthrough separately reproduces a WiredTiger panic after changing database-file ownership. These examples defeat a universal invariant-to-corruption mapping. (medium confidence)

Historical Percona 4.4.9 release notes distinguish WT-7426, WT-7995 and WT-7984 by affected versions, failure mechanisms and remediation. They describe validation and possible initial sync for particular defects; they do not justify a blanket 'WiredTiger invariant => restore PITR or resync' prescription for Atlas. (low confidence)

SERVER-35031 records historical reuse of code 50 for timeouts unrelated to maxTimeMS, which could produce an ExecutionTimeout exception even when an application had not set maxTimeMS. The ticket records fixes in 4.0.1 and 4.1.2; this historical scope does not establish that every current code-50 error has the same cause. (low confidence)

Before adopting a known-issue remedy, match the observed version and specific failure evidence. Percona reproduces SERVER-13751 on MongoDB 2.6.0; a separate startup investigation records version 3.4.18, the assertion source location and KVCatalog::init frames. This supports evidence-specific matching rather than treating a generic SERVER project link as a diagnosis. (medium confidence)

Percona recommends matching a clear crash stack and exact binary version to a specific bug, and supplying a reproduction when available. In its SERVER-13751 example, the fix validates calling arguments rather than modifying the function appearing at the failure site; a stack frame alone does not identify the repair. (low confidence)

For client-side operation timeout handling, the driver specification identifies MaxTimeMSExpired by numeric code 50, not by message or codeName; it can occur at top level, inside writeErrors, or inside writeConcernError. (low confidence)

Do not infer that an application's explicit maxTimeMS setting caused every code-50 event. SERVER-35031 documents historical reuse outside maxTimeMS, while a MongoDB 6.0.6 community report shows a MirrorMaestro connection with maxTimeMS:1000 although the reporter's application did not set it. These are scoped examples, not proof of a current Atlas defect. (medium confidence)

The IC2E 2023 researchers tested a synchronization issue using MongoDB 6.0 and WiredTiger 10.0.2 with deliberately constrained CPU affinity and altered thread priorities. They evaluated a modified backoff implementation. The paper explicitly leaves Atlas connection-control behavior uncertain; it does not establish a verified Atlas production fix. (low confidence)

Methodological synthesis: a KB entry should retain the observed signature, tested software version, reproduction conditions, and evidence supporting the proposed fix. The differing scopes of a reproduced crash and a controlled synchronization experiment support treating KB matches as hypotheses until the deployment's conditions match. (medium confidence)
